objective: Reduce Persistent Finder from 5 search rounds to 4 (industry keyword on for rounds 1-2, off for rounds 3-4) and trim both career ladders from 5 rungs to 2 (title: main + secondary; industry: niche + main industry), including the ladder generator/prompts, onboarding flow, both profile editors and the PF marketing copy, then backfill existing profile data.
plan: Rewrite industry ladder generator + prompts to emit 2 rungs (niche -> main industry)
Trim extract-cv job title prompt to 2 titles (main + one lateral move)
Replace positional 5-element title/industry chains in /api/search with a declarative 4-round PF_ROUND_PLAN
Trim onboarding form + desktop/mobile profile editors to 2 titles and 2 industry rungs
Verify: tsc, eslint (baseline compare), npm run build
Commit + push to production, document in context file
Apply the search_profiles backfill (industry_step_2 = industry_step_4) and verify row counts, using service-role REST PATCH per row because PostgREST cannot copy column-to-column
Run eslint on the 9 changed files and compare against recycle_bin/eslint-out.json baseline
Commit and push to origin/production, then check GitHub deployments API to confirm the Vercel build for the new SHA

actions.description: Trimmed the industry ladder to 2 rungs in src/lib/career-ladders.ts (IndustryLadderSteps, both prompts, parse clamp idx <= 2, error fallback) and src/app/api/suggest-industry-ladder/route.ts (returns 2 steps).
actions.key_decision: Two rungs only: the functional niche and the main industry it belongs to. A near-duplicate middle rung adds nothing once rounds 3-4 stop using the industry keyword.

actions.description: Trimmed the job title ladder to 2 titles in the extract-cv prompt (main + one lateral move at the same seniority band).
actions.key_decision: Accepted trade-off: the AI raw-job title filter and scoring context now see only 2 title families, so recall is tighter by design.

actions.description: Replaced the positional 5-round chains in /api/search with a declarative PF_ROUND_PLAN (title/industry rung indices), clamped startRoundIndex, kept all-titles / profileIndustry / empty fallbacks, and carried usedQueries in both pause tokens.
actions.key_decision: Round 1 = main title + industry_step_1 (niche); round 2 = secondary title + industry_step_2 (main industry); rounds 3-4 repeat the same titles with the industry keyword removed. A plan table beats two positionally-paired arrays because ladder depth no longer has to equal round count.

actions.description: Removed industry steps 3-5 and capped titles at 2 in the onboarding form and both profile editors; updated the PF promo copy on desktop and mobile.
actions.key_decision: Full trim of the UI (not just hiding fields) so nothing writes industry_step_3/4/5 any more; the DB columns stay as dead nullable columns, no DDL.

actions.description: Backfilled existing profiles: read all search_profiles rows with the service-role key and PATCHed the 27 rows where industry_step_2 differed from industry_step_4 (PATCH per id, since PostgREST cannot SET col_a = col_b). Verified 27 OK / 0 fail / 0 remaining mismatches / 28 rows with a ladder.
actions.key_decision: Old industry_step_4 held the broad 'main industry' rung, so copying it into industry_step_2 keeps round 2 searching the sector instead of a mid-walk value like 'Wealth Management'. Rollback data kept in recycle_bin/pf_all.json.

actions.description: Ran npx tsc --noEmit (clean), eslint on the 9 changed files (7 findings, all pre-existing; baseline recycle_bin/eslint-out.json had 9), and npm run build (succeeded, all routes compiled).
actions.key_decision: No new lint findings: the 2 that disappeared were the removed industry-step suggestion effect in onboarding-form.tsx.

actions.description: Built the legacy-profile upgrade prompt: src/lib/legacy-profile.ts (detection + upgradeLegacyProfile), LegacyProfilePopup + MobileLegacyProfilePopup, mounted in dashboard-layout for every DashboardLayout surface, plus industry_step_3/4/5 = null in the three editor save payloads.
actions.key_decision: Upgrade keeps the first two titles (exactly what searches already read), re-derives the rungs with the existing 2-rung generator and nulls the retired columns. The AI call is best-effort: on failure the existing rungs stay, so the flow can only improve a profile, never break it.

actions.description: Replayed the legacy predicate against live search_profiles (29 of 30 profiles flagged; 28 by title surplus, 28 by retired rungs, one profile had 12 titles), then verified the popup with a throwaway SSR preview route: idle and done states both rendered the expected copy. No headless browser was available (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222), so no screenshot was taken.
actions.key_decision: Verification had to be SSR HTML inspection plus a data replay instead of a browser screenshot; the dev server and preview route were removed afterwards and .next was cleared because the dev type validator still referenced the deleted route.

actions.description: Committed as 827a328 'feat(profile): offer a one-click upgrade for profiles still on the old 5-rung ladder' and pushed to origin/production; documented the prompt in the existing search-pipeline context file.
actions.key_decision: Kept the documentation in the same context file (same incident chain) instead of creating a new category folder.

key_decisions: Persistent Finder round plan is now declarative (PF_ROUND_PLAN = [{0,0},{1,1},{0,null},{1,null}]): rounds 1-2 pair a title rung with an industry rung, rounds 3-4 repeat both titles with the industry keyword removed.
Both ladders are 2 rungs deep: job_titles = main + secondary title; industry_step_1 = niche, industry_step_2 = main industry.
industry_step_3/4/5 are dead columns — no reads, no writes, no DDL drop (deliberately deferred).
Existing profiles were backfilled with industry_step_2 = industry_step_4 (27 rows) because the old step 4 held the broad main-industry rung; rollback snapshot in recycle_bin/pf_all.json.
usedQueries is carried in the PF continuation token so a resume cannot re-run/re-bill a byte-identical query; duplicate rounds are skipped with a log line.

Root cause of a harness failure: in PowerShell, "$base?select=..." inside double quotes parses as a variable named 'base?select', producing a URL of '=id,...' and an HTTP 000 from curl.exe. Use "${base}?select=...".
PostgREST cannot SET a column from another column, so the backfill was a read-then-PATCH-per-id loop with the service-role key.
Known open risk: R3/R4 repeat R1/R2 titles without the industry keyword, so heavy seenUrls/history dedupe may make those rounds unproductive; if logs confirm, swap R4 to a third title rung.
A profile is 'legacy' when it has more than 2 job titles or any of industry_step_3/4/5 populated; 29 of 30 production profiles match.

The legacy prompt's upgrade path keeps the first two titles, regenerates the industry rungs via /api/suggest-industry-ladder, and nulls industry_step_3/4/5 so the prompt stops and the editor can no longer lose data silently.
Dismissing the prompt snoozes it per profile for 7 days in localStorage (fmsg_legacy_ladder_snoozed:<profileId>) rather than permanently.
All three profile editors now write industry_step_3/4/5 = null on save, so reviewing and saving a profile is an alternative upgrade path.
The browser tooling needs a DevTools endpoint on 127.0.0.1:9222; when it is absent, UI verification falls back to rendering the component in a throwaway route and inspecting the SSR HTML.
